summary: This cross-sectional study evaluated the relationship between ocular axial length and retinal nerve fiber layer and ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness in 120 eyes of 60 healthy participants using spectral optical coherence tomography (OCT)-Cirrus HD-OCT. Before correcting for ocular magnification, a significant negative correlation was found between axial length and retinal nerve fiber layer thickness in all quadrants, as well as ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness. After adjusting for magnification using Littmann's formula, a positive correlation was observed between axial length and temporal retinal nerve fiber layer thickness and average ganglion cell-inner plexiform layer thickness.
